status: D1-D39 fully ratified; D40 B selected, details proposed; no Q41
evidence_class: Exact read-only source and accepted local-document captures. No runtime/DB/provider proof. Uncommitted grooming documents pinned by actual bytes, not asserted to exist at HEAD.

evidence.heading: ### D3-R01 — Four mutually exclusive meanings and mixed waits
evidence.text:
### D3-R01 — Four mutually exclusive meanings and mixed waits

“A conversation has exactly one authoritative current work meaning. Open means Support currently owes a substantive next step or a due review/follow-up, including reviewing new input. Waiting for requester means requested information/action from admitted people seeking support is the remaining active blocker. Waiting on our side means a necessary input already sought from a colleague, owning-domain process or outside party is outstanding and Support retains responsibility for obtaining it. Resolved is an explicit completion of the Support obligation, not simply read, out of the inbox or no immediate response needed.”

“If Support currently owes a substantive next step or a due review/follow-up, use Open. Merely being able to send an optional progress update does not end a genuine wait. Otherwise, if an active our-side blocker remains, use Waiting on our side, including mixed requester/our-side waits. Use Waiting for requester only when the remaining active blocker is requester-side. Preserve additional context in existing notes or permitted owner references; do not introduce a fifth Mixed status, mandatory blocker taxonomy or dependency graph. Hypothetical future tasks are not active blockers. An inability to determine the correct wait calls for staff review, not inferred resolution or a fifth normal state.”

evidence.heading: ### D3-R02 — Intent and causal evidence, never message direction
evidence.text:
### D3-R02 — Intent and causal evidence, never message direction

“A staff progress update, note, read action, assignment, CRM link or queued email does not itself choose Waiting or Resolved. Work changes follow explicit authorized staff intent or a qualified causal event under this contract. A required requester question can support Waiting for requester; an ‘I am investigating’ update leaves the obligation with Support. Delivery is shown separately: queued, retrying, failed, suppressed or indeterminate mail is not proof that anyone received a question.”

“Requester-side input may come from a legitimately admitted participant other than the original requester or CRM-linked address. Matching email, quoted headers or a conversation reference alone do not establish that admission or protected-action authority. A waiting label does not add recipients, subscribe anyone, create a Party or change the D2 draft audience. Sending a progress update while genuinely awaiting another input is allowed; sending alone does not change the wait.”

evidence.heading: ### D3-R05 — Current state and durable history
evidence.text:
### D3-R05 — Current state and durable history

“Maintain a current work snapshot plus append-only authoritative transition evidence. Each actual change records prior/new meaning, cause, trusted human/system actor, server admission/order, command/event identity and permitted causal reference in the same transaction. Source occurrence time, where useful, is separate from server admission order. Reopen preserves the prior resolution episode; repeat Resolve against already resolved work does not create a new completion or replace its timestamp.”

“Current-state counts, time in a waiting episode, elapsed unresolved time and completed resolution episodes are distinct measures. A message, progress update, CRM edit or inbox move cannot reset a wait period merely because it changed `updated_at`. A requester-to-our-side change records the old episode's end and new side's start. Historical corrections append lineage; they do not silently rewrite earlier history. Work-status changes do not themselves emit duplicate external communication events into Phase 6.”

Use current snapshot plus transition evidence, not wholesale event sourcing. Existing mutable `resolved_at` may remain a projection if needed for compatibility; it cannot be the sole historical authority. Redaction and retention still follow D1 and their owners, not a blanket promise to retain every body forever.

evidence.heading: ### D3-R08 — New input, failures and resolution eligibility
evidence.text:
### D3-R08 — New input, failures and resolution eligibility

“A first-time admitted relevant human reply returns the conversation to Open for review and invalidates its obsolete deferral, even if the sender's timestamp predates a prior resolution. Durable intake/effect identity prevents duplicate delivery from reopening work again. Automated, quarantined, malicious, unrelated or already-applied intake is not a human work transition. A newly available result for the current awaited authorized owner action also creates review work; stale/superseded references do not blindly change status.”

“Fresh adverse evidence requiring staff investigation—such as a relevant unresolved delivery failure or ambiguous outcome—creates Open review work through the same causal boundary, including after a prior resolution. Preserve the prior resolution as history; this does not declare it dishonest retrospectively. Do not reopen for every duplicate callback or an already-reviewed/provably superseded result. When relevance cannot safely be established, retain visible qualified review work rather than silently discard the evidence. Provider/member evidence remains under D1/D2.”

“Resolve is deliberate and cannot hide a known outstanding Support obligation, promised follow-up or required unreviewed recovery action. It does not certify receipt/read status or complete a giving/CRM/document/care action. Pending automated delivery remains separately visible and recoverable; a later failure may create new review work. No required donor courtesy acknowledgement is added after an otherwise complete answer. Reading, adding a note or completing an owner UI is never implicit resolution.”

No arbitrary no-response timeout, irreversible Closed stage, automatic closure email, SLA pause or default Send-and-resolve behavior is selected by D3. An explicit future Send-and-status convenience must expose both effects and satisfy the same approval, transaction and recovery contracts. User-selected work intent must not be replaced by text classification or AI guessing.

evidence.heading: ### D4-R03 — Atomic local admission, honest asynchronous outcome
evidence.text:
### D4-R03 — Atomic local admission, honest asynchronous outcome

“Use one server-authorized Support admission boundary for the reviewed reply and optional work action. It derives scope and actor from authenticated context, verifies exact target/audience/content and relevant revisions, validates the selected D3 transition, and commits the immutable command identity/hash, Support message intent, work/history/reminder effects and durable dispatch/recovery intent atomically. Validation or a stale review before admission creates neither the reply nor the combined work effect. No sequence of independent browser requests may implement Send and resolve.”

“Before local admission, the exact human-reply candidate is fully server-validated and compiled under pinned dependencies, matches the reviewed digest and has durable ready preparation. Preparation may be staged before the local transaction, but unadmitted artifacts have no dispatch authority. Admission atomically claims that exact ready preparation and records the reply, any work effect, history and dispatch intent. No unresolved variable, first-time rendering or unqualified template choice is deferred until after Send-and-resolve has committed. Actual dispatch still checks live authorization and safety fences. There is no database transaction around Resend I/O. A failure after local admission remains an admitted message with visible recovery evidence; it cannot pretend the chosen work transition never happened. A fresh actionable execution/safety/delivery problem creates D3 Open review causally, without replaying old work intent.”

“Ordinary preflight problems are identified before admission when knowable. Local success is labelled Queued, not delivered. A lost response first reconciles the durable command identity, preserving the draft as pending recovery; it does not mint a new send because the browser timed out.”

evidence.heading: ### D4-R09 — Immutable preparation and exact provider envelope
evidence.text:
### D4-R09 — Immutable preparation and exact provider envelope

“Reuse ADR-0032's permanent occurrence slot and complete semantic/command hash checks. Same identity and same immutable input reconcile the existing effect; changed input conflicts; a genuinely new deliberate reply has a new authorized identity even when its text is identical. Freeze the approved content, complete source/presentation/compiler/locale dependencies, exact recipients and attachments, owner/connection/sender/reply revisions and preparation hashes before delivery authority.”

“Phase 6 seals the exact endpoint, request bytes, permitted headers, account/credential revision, ordered member relationship and one request-level Resend idempotency key before I/O. That provider key is created when the envelope is sealed, not used as the permanent business identity. Send prepared HTML and plain text; do not invoke a mutable Resend template ID/alias or re-render React/template content at dispatch. Provider-hosted templates are a legitimate external feature but introduce a second rendering/publication authority that this contract does not need.”

“ADR-0032's strict batch rules continue to govern independent messages. The D2 native group contract is a separately qualified shape, not an assumption that batch support proves group safety. No sealed or possibly submitted envelope is split, rechunked, rekeyed or moved to another account.”

evidence.heading: ### D4-R11 — Bounded recovery, never blind resending
evidence.text:
### D4-R11 — Bounded recovery, never blind resending

“Preserve ADR-0032's three recovery conditions: unprepared, prepared definitely unsubmitted and may have submitted. An accepted response requires a valid provider message identity and an exact envelope/member match. A malformed success, missing identity, transport ambiguity or contradictory mapping is not proof of no send. Once I/O may have happened, only the contract's specifically allowed concurrent-idempotency, typed provider-5xx or network/timeout conditions permit an identical same-key follow-up, without contradictory evidence.”

“The sealed envelope has at most two follow-up HTTP calls after its initial call in total, within the provider key window, frozen earliest deadline and live safety fences, with the governed jitter/Retry-After behavior. All attempts preserve exact endpoint, bytes, order, account, credential, headers and key. Mapping uncertainty, payload conflict, drift or exhausted allowance becomes reconciliation-only/Delivery outcome unknown. Do not convert a generic SDK error string into definite rejection, issue a new key on conflict, rerender an updated template or replay after the provider window.”

“User Undo is never mail recall. An unsubmitted cancellation, if offered by the governed contract, requires a conditional fence before I/O; if that cannot be proved, show the true outcome and retain recovery. This decision does not add a new cancellable-send product.”

evidence.heading: ### D5-R01 — Meaning and proportionate eligibility
evidence.text:
### D5-R01 — Meaning and proportionate eligibility

“No response is the reason staff deliberately ended further Support follow-up because clearly requested needed input remains absent. It is not a count of human messages or proof of refusal, neglect, delivery, satisfaction or an achieved business outcome. Identify the current remaining need using existing authorized conversation context and references to the relevant request and latest reviewed input; do not add a generic blocker graph or require a long new form.”

“New relevant partial information or an acknowledgement first creates D3 review and invalidates an older ending approval. After review, staff may retain a clearly still-unanswered portion of the existing request as the basis for a later ending; another chaser email is not mandatory merely to requalify it. If the required information has arrived, the requester explicitly declined or cannot supply it, withdrew the request, or asked staff a new clarification question, do not silently treat that response as the same no-response basis. Handle the actual current work. ‘No further response’ may explain the situation in prose, but does not create a second disposition.”

“Use the same four D3 work meanings. Eligibility follows current reviewed obligations, not only the current Waiting for requester label: due reminders may already have made the conversation Open. An active our-side Support obligation prevents this ending; the mere existence of an unrelated linked owner-domain process does not. Ordinary completion still needs no requester courtesy acknowledgement after an otherwise complete answer.”

evidence.heading: ### D5-R03 — Commitments and domain authority
evidence.text:
### D5-R03 — Commitments and domain authority

“An ending cannot waive a known required Support action, promise, currently relevant owner obligation that Support must follow through on, or required unreviewed recovery. Use the existing owner-authorized status/action/reference contracts for known guards. Check necessary owner evidence under current permissions; unavailable required evidence is not success. Explain a blocked or unavailable review without exposing restricted details.”

“Do not scan every CRM relationship or pretend software can prove the meaning of every free-text promise. Server-enforced known facts and accountable human review serve different roles. No mandatory checkbox substitutes for owner authorization, and no new generic task/claim/approval engine is required. Authorized correction remains possible without claiming that audit alone prevents deliberate misuse.”

“Support owns its work status, ending record and conversation. CRM owns Parties and relationships; giving, receipts/documents, recurring gifts, refunds and member-care retain their own permissions, validation, approval, completion and audit. End follow-up does not cancel or dismiss those owner records. A support assignment, requester link or conversation membership never grants access to them. Care-classified content retains its Phase 38 boundary; No response is not a way to move it into the general inbox.”

evidence.heading: ### D10-R02 — Original evidence and a reversible handling relationship
evidence.text:
### D10-R02 — Original evidence and a reversible handling relationship

“Keep each original conversation ID, its source messages, original endpoints/headers/times, attachment custody, source business references and history stable. Each original conversation belongs to exactly one current handling component. Its current root is the continuing conversation; there is no second copied ticket or mutable transcript store.”

“Represent active merges as a narrow rooted forest: a source root has at most one active parent; a root has no active parent; cycles and self-merge are forbidden. Merge only current distinct roots, adding one operation-owned active edge from the source root to the explicitly chosen continuing root. Ended edges remain audit evidence. A materialized root lookup is a derived acceleration, not write authority.”

“An old URL is resolved visibly through current handling before a new action is reviewed. Cached root IDs or permanent redirects cannot freeze that relationship after Undo; navigation requalifies current topology and access. Selecting an original already in the same component reports Already combined; it does not create another edge. Re-merging after Undo creates a new edge/generation and receipt. Original source identity and current handling identity remain distinct in every API and projection.”

evidence.heading: ### D10-R07 — Source-aware future email and correlation
evidence.text:
### D10-R07 — Source-aware future email and correlation

“Every admitted message/recovery effect retains its immutable source identity. Resolve its original thread/source from qualified owner correlation, then resolve current handling atomically with the D3 effect. If input wins before Undo, the Undo preview includes it; if Undo wins, the input creates work in the resulting current component. Replayed original effects do not open both sides.”

“Preserve original Message-ID, In-Reply-To, References and approved reply-route provenance. A reply to either original conversation continues in the root while merged and follows its original current component after separation. Conflicting or insufficient original-source evidence remains in the existing durable thread/route-review path; even references resolving to the same current root must not erase ambiguity needed for later correction. No arbitrary first match or current-root guess replaces source evidence.”

“Unrelated new email without qualified thread evidence remains new serviceable intake. A past merge does not authorize sender/subject auto-adoption. Resend transports and reports mail facts; Support owns current handling. The donor's external mailbox may retain two old threads. No promise is made to rewrite external mailbox history.”

evidence.heading: ### D10-R08 — Drafts, replies, Email Studio and admitted sends
evidence.text:
### D10-R08 — Drafts, replies, Email Studio and admitted sends

“A reply retains its exact reviewed target-message/original-source lineage and D2 audience. Opening combined handling neither unions participants nor quotes source history into an external reply. P17/Email Studio preparation and P6/Resend effects keep their original sender, author, content, attachment authority, relation set and idempotency identity.”

“Preserve private draft text and ownership. A topology change invalidates unsafe stale send admission through current controls; it does not discard text, transfer a draft to the assignee or silently retarget it. After refresh, staff deliberately review the current exact message and audience. Already admitted or possibly submitted effects are reconciled under their original identity, not rekeyed, resent, reassigned or falsely recalled. Current owner revocation remains independently capable of blocking unsent provider I/O.”

“While merged, relevant unseen updates from any constituent source participate in the one current component's send-collision guard. Drafts opened through different original URLs cannot pass independent source-only guards and send competing replies to the same combined work.”

“Late delivery/adverse evidence remains attached to the original effect and opens review at current qualified handling when relevant. A merge cannot hide a queued/bounced/unknown send or claim that a successful member represents every recipient.”

evidence.heading: ### D10-R09 — One work outcome without manufactured completion
evidence.text:
### D10-R09 — One work outcome without manufactured completion

“Merge presents one resulting current D3 work plan. Open dominates when any source owes action or required review; matching waits may retain that meaning; mixed blocking waits use Waiting on our side when no immediate action is owed, as D3 already requires. Both legitimately complete sources may remain Resolved. Staff can select another currently valid plan only through the same explicit D3 authority and obligation checks.”

“The absorbed source becomes handled in the continuing conversation, not a newly successful resolution or No response ending. Preserve its historical work episodes and facts; no hidden legacy Resolved write may trigger closure mail, success reporting or D5 automation. New work from either original source remains visible. Merge cannot swallow an outstanding Support promise, required recovery or unreviewed owner outcome associated with a financial action. An independent owner process retains its own state and need not keep Support work Open.”

evidence.heading: ### D10-R12 — Undo the selected relationship, including later merges
evidence.text:
### D10-R12 — Undo the selected relationship, including later merges

“Provide persistent Undo merge for each still-active merge relationship. Undo ends that exact edge and detaches its current source subtree. It preserves other active relationships, later independent edits and original evidence. No arbitrary time limit, page-session lifetime, one-use toast or latest-merge-only restriction makes ordinary separation unavailable.”

“For B→A then A→C, Undo B→A separates B and its still-attached descendants from C while A/C remain together. Undo A→C separates A and its still-attached descendants from C. A descendant previously separated does not return; a later source merged into current root C stays there. Preview names the two actual resulting components, not the obsolete pair from the original receipt. A new merge selected through an old alias uses the visible current root.”

“Undo is a currently authorized compensating command, not restoration of a whole old graph or record snapshot. Current source retention may remove payload while structural separation remains possible. If present authority is missing, route to the qualified existing owner/administrator recovery path without revealing protected content or requiring routine direct SQL repair.”

evidence.heading: ### D14-R11 — No reply needed and honest endings
evidence.text:
### D14-R11 — No reply needed and honest endings

Provide an explicit, current-revision **No reply needed** disposition for the exact reviewed outstanding contributions, for cases such as an acknowledgment while internal work continues. It marks only those exact contributions as needing no reply; it preserves any uncovered older/newer inputs, D3 work/reminders/owner actions and creates no sent event or response credit. Removing a complete oldest prefix starts the remaining collecting period from its own oldest input and stored policy bundle without inventing human First fulfillment; removing a non-prefix cannot reset the older owed deadline. Preserve already-confirmed misses for the disposed portion. It cannot settle a known outstanding promised reply or unreviewed actionable recovery merely to clear a target. Use current source/obligation review, not text classification. New input after the reviewed cutoff remains owed.

An eligible D3 Resolve can end remaining no-longer-owed reply periods in the same approved command rather than force a redundant second action. No response, continued elsewhere and created in error retain their distinct D5/D12 meanings. D12 transferred work follows R15 rather than being ended for reporting. Before-due no-reply/withdrawal is an explicit exclusion, never met; after a known miss that miss remains alongside the eventual disposition. A source-owned correction proving mistaken eligibility/time can revise results with audit; ordinary late cleanup cannot improve the denominator. Persistent Undo no reply needed reverses only the still-current mistaken disposition for the exact still-unfulfilled contribution set, through a new authorized correction and contribution/source fences. Preserve original age/policy, reconcile with the current collecting period and create current review with a new generation, without duplicate active periods or restoring old status/reminder snapshots. Already accepted-covered contributions are a no-op; newer input is untouched. Independent Off/withdrawal remains effective, so restoring reply work does not re-enable its stopped target. A valid restored target uses its original due/history interpretation, with any resulting miss/correction explicit. Undo never cancels admitted mail.

evidence.heading: ### D14-R24 — Attribution and historical integrity
evidence.text:
### D14-R24 — Attribution and historical integrity

Current assignee/inbox filters are legitimate for current workload when labelled **Currently assigned/handled by**. They cannot rewrite the responding actor, original source, policy-at-start or custody-at-due dimensions. Record historical responsibility references and reply actor evidence under their own owners, including Shared and unavailable hydration without inventing a person. A response spanning several scoped obligations does not become several emails or hours of labor. Multi-tenant/CRM merges, source relinking, staff departure and calendar changes never rewrite past events or create duplicate authoritative state.

Historical source corrections append revision/cause/evidence; reports disclose the applied interpretation and As of/generated-at version. A previously generated export remains its captured snapshot, not silently edited history. Report access is evaluated currently; preserving attribution never preserves revoked access to private content. Do not introduce individual leaderboards, donation-weighted response performance or claims about staff productivity from queue assignment alone.

evidence.heading: ### D15-R05 — Stop, re-follow, access loss and ordinary endings
evidence.text:
### D15-R05 — Stop, re-follow, access loss and ordinary endings

Follow persists across Open, both Waiting categories, ordinary Resolve, manual reassignment, coverage and inbox moves while exact source/staff authority remains valid. It is not a duty and does not need an active task. A later genuinely new permitted contribution can therefore update a follower of a resolved conversation. Following a currently resolved conversation is allowed and future-only; it does not replay its history.

Stop ends new optional selection and unsent authorization for those generations. It also ends unread treatment for already-available follow-only information through an explicit source-applicability correction, without inventing a read. Authorized recent history remains under its original P17 limits. Already-authorized in-flight/accepted email cannot be recalled. Stop never changes shared status, reminder, reply coverage, assignment, delegated work or a separately qualified direct/required attention reason. Re-follow starts a new generation/frontier and never restores old unread debt, canceled deliveries or stopped generations.

Confirmed loss of the relevant staff/source access, account retirement or source retirement closes only affected generations and removes active/recent presentation under ADR0027. Later regrant requires a new deliberate Follow and cannot transfer old role-scoped notices. An authorization outage or indeterminate identity lookup fails closed temporarily; it is not proof to permanently end intent. Stop remains available through a safe self-owned cleanup command without disclosing an inaccessible source. A source-scope erasure/correction applies the owning retention/privacy policy; it does not fabricate another request or user.

evidence.heading: ### D15-R06 — Finite useful activity set
evidence.text:
### D15-R06 — Finite useful activity set

Only the following source-qualified classes create optional following information. Qualification uses actual original/affected source scope and immutable occurrence identity. Repeated webhook or projection writes are not new human activity.

| Class | Included occurrence                                                                  | Required boundary                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| E1    | A newly qualified human inbound contribution becomes Support-ready                   | Preserve original receipt time and first qualified admission separately. No quarantined/unqualified body, suspected automation, duplicate input, forwarded unrelated content or attachment-progress notice. Input that also reopens work creates one contribution update with truthful context.                 |
| E2    | A genuine human Support reply receives qualified P6 acceptance evidence              | Preserve actual original message/effect and qualified recipient/member meaning. Queued/draft/unknown/automatic mail cannot become a sent-human update. Show partial recipient evidence honestly. A transferred reply remains its native original; D14 coverage of another original is not follower inheritance. |
| E3    | A human internal note is published                                                   | Current permission for that exact note is required. A system summary, event row or scan is not human publication. Edits/redaction correct existing presentation under R08, without a new alert for every edit.                                                                                                  |
| E4    | A deliberate human work ending or reopening, including truthful D12 Continued ending | Describe Support's actual ending reason, not completion of a refund or other domain. Use the exact affected-source set for a component-wide action. Created-in-error retirement is correction/end-of-authority, not a new successful outcome notice.                                                            |

Routine assignment/coverage/inbox/Waiting/label/priority edits update current work views without an optional follower notice. D14 due Open, reminder/timer processing, delivery tracking, scans, retries, Follow/Stop, notification engagement and unrelated CRM/Party/task activity do not enter this set. Required custody, assistance, recovery or direct-mention attention remains governed by its own producer. A staff action with an explanatory note and work ending may form one qualified source episode while preserving its distinct facts; closeness in time alone is insufficient.

evidence.heading: ### D16-R01 — Need, scope and strongest alternative
evidence.text:
### D16-R01 — Need, scope and strongest alternative

Allow correction of accidentally included private material while keeping the legitimate request usable. The illustrative receipt question with an unrelated private paragraph and wrong attachment tests this need; it is not measured ministry demand. B, whole affected body/file removal, is the strongest simpler alternative and remains a deliberate fallback. C, retaining a revealable masked original, adds custody and reveal risk without an established ordinary Support need. A is accepted with the safeguards below, not because competitors establish universal best practice.

The feature applies to retained original incoming messages, published internal notes and sent-reply representations that Support owns, including eligible closed/archived conversation sources. It is not a general edit-history feature or authority to rewrite another author's statement. Draft editing remains its own operation. Do not require reopening a conversation, changing assignment, or creating a ticket in another domain merely to correct content.

evidence.heading: ### D16-R03 — Exact original scope and source representations
evidence.text:
### D16-R03 — Exact original scope and source representations

Each operation targets one original message identity, its reviewed current content revision, explicit text ranges/whole fields and selected attachment occurrences. Multiple disjoint ranges in that one message are permitted. It does not target a changing merged root or a search query that can acquire new results. A source-owned representation inventory identifies canonical body, alternate text/HTML, parsed intake copy, raw MIME, attachments and managed derivatives. It must cover the current inbound duplication observed in Core.

Apply selected redaction to every equivalent representation of the selected original. If raw MIME or an alternate body cannot be safely transformed with proven correspondence, remove/restrict that whole representation through its owner; do not keep a secret-bearing “View original email” escape hatch. Explicitly disclose loss of original-format viewing in the review. Independent quoted messages or newly forwarded messages are distinct evidence; they require reviewed additional operations or the broader applicable privacy process, not a claim that every occurrence everywhere was erased.

evidence.heading: ### D17-R04 — Stable original content and active-purpose eligibility
evidence.text:
### D17-R04 — Stable original content and active-purpose eligibility

Retirement binds a bounded content generation/frontier of one original Support source. It never deletes a changing merged-root query result or the entire conversation row. A generation covers all Support-owned content admitted through that frontier, including automatic confirmations and generated/system-note content and their files/representations, with original identities and monotonic admission ordering. Human content is the limited renewal class, not the only content subject to expiry. Typed content-free control facts retain their separate policy. Pre-qualified intake/quarantine material remains with its actual owner and shorter limits. A generation is not a new CRM person or necessarily a new conversation each time content expires.

Normal eligibility requires ended Support work plus absence of a qualified continuing Support need for that original content. D3 Open and both Waiting categories remain unfinished. D10 merged-away status does not prove finished purpose while the duplicate-work component still handles the issue. D12 Continued endings and D11 delegated work require their exact source-interest/obligation checks. A Finance task merely existing, a peer-related conversation, Party link, follower or citation is neither an indefinite hold nor disposal authority. Retain only the explicit source scope genuinely needed by ongoing work; no recursive whole-CRM retention graph.

evidence.heading: ### D17-R05 — Precise inactivity anchor
evidence.text:
### D17-R05 — Precise inactivity anchor

For an unexpired content generation, the ordinary anchor is the later of its latest genuine relevant Support-purpose ending and its latest first durable admission of native human content. Count only qualified human incoming content becoming Support-ready, a human reply admitted for sending through the qualified Core command, and a newly published human internal note. Count the event once. Draft typing, unsent preparation alone, automatic confirmations, generated/system notes, note edits, redaction, expiry, delivery callbacks, imports of duplicates, reads, assignments, labels, links, merge/Undo and repeat identical Resolve do not move the anchor.

Do not wait for or use P6 provider acceptance as the retention activity clock: deliberately admitted reply content can exist while delivery is unknown. P6 actual send/delivery evidence stays separate and truthful. Provider/email Date, backdated user text and worker execution time cannot replace first qualified source admission. A genuinely new human note on ended work is new content and updates inactivity; no AI semantic test tries to decide whether it was meaningful. Oldest-content purpose review and mandatory owner ceilings address repeated chatter retaining older context.

If continuing purpose ends later, record that real ending once and use its time; repeated status commands are no-ops for this clock. A status-only correction or reopen–resolve cycle without a new qualified purpose preserves the prior anchor; mechanically cycling status is not new work evidence. If note editing is supported, saving edits keeps that content's existing deadline and must not imply a renewed lifetime. Legacy dates that cannot prove the anchor remain explicitly unknown and require bounded reconciliation, not created_at guessing, a fresh retention lifetime on migration or immediate destruction.

evidence.heading: ### D17-R10 — Policy changes cannot reverse elapsed authority
evidence.text:
### D17-R10 — Policy changes cannot reverse elapsed authority

Let d be the source's already-authoritative expiry deadline. An authorized policy change or qualifying new work admitted at E strictly before d may affect future eligibility/deadline. At E equal to or after d, the old content has expired even if no worker has yet nulled a body or deleted an object. Process that expired frontier before admitting new content or applying an extension; it cannot be rescued by worker lag, policy lengthening, reopening, an inbox move or Undo.

Conversely, an extension validly effective before d must be honored even when a due-date projection still contains the old deadline. A stale worker must not destroy content using the old version. Evaluate policy-version history, source events and purpose state at the relevant authority boundary; a current-value-only setting plus best-effort mass row updates is insufficient. Current source authority may be computed lazily or projected, but every read/mutation/disposal must qualify it against the actual effective revisions. No giant cross-tenant transaction is required.

evidence.heading: ### D17-R19 — Prepared material and the send race
evidence.text:
### D17-R19 — Prepared material and the send race

Existing source-derived quotes, files, destinations and prepared material lose applicable read/decrypt/send authority when their source frontier expires. Preserve unrelated authored work where it can be separated safely; otherwise require clean current review. Never silently replace frozen bytes or submit a cleaned message on the user's behalf. A later expired-source autosave cannot repopulate the old quote.

P6 `dispatching` remains the I/O boundary. Source expiry before new dispatch admission blocks the attempt; a send authorized earlier may already be in flight/accepted/unknown. Preserve that evidence without a recall claim; deny later payload-bearing retries after the source stop. ADR0032 sealed envelopes cannot be split/rerendered/rekeyed, including when only one member's source expired. Fresh review alone cannot justify replacing an accepted or indeterminate send. Preserve the existing 24-hour prepared execution-material purge rule after authority removal and any earlier owner deadline; the tenant retention period never extends it.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R08 — One deliberate release
evidence.text:
### D19-R08 — One deliberate release

In the preview, show **Release to [inbox]** with the qualified destination and whether intake will create a new conversation or continue an identified authorized conversation. If that outcome is not yet provable, say it will be checked during processing; never promise “new ticket” or silently attach to an arbitrary record. Show concise scope copy: “Only this message. Future mail rules stay the same.” An explicit review of this summary is the ordinary confirmation; do not add a second generic “Are you sure?” dialog when scope is unchanged. Admit a source-version-bound decision, recheck every gate and record one durable processing obligation. Show **Release requested** until canonical admission is proven, then **Released** with the authorized destination link. Release is not Send, Resolve, registration, email verification, allowlisting, a refund or any other business action. When D13 confirmation may still apply, show “The usual new-request confirmation may follow if this message is eligible”; never promise no email can follow admission.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R10 — Dismissal and correction
evidence.text:
### D19-R10 — Dismissal and correction

**Dismiss** means “Keep this message out of Support work.” It records one typed reason and removes the item from To review; it neither blocks future mail nor deletes a CRM contact or immediately destroys content. Show “Recoverable until [exact original deadline]” and a persistent **Return to review** action in History while current authority and content lifetime permit. A transient Undo can invoke that same command, but is never the only recovery route. Returning to review does not release, renew content retention or clear safety gates. At expiry the action becomes unavailable with an honest explanation; no background lag extends the recovery promise. Preserve Dismissed as the historical decision and Content expired as current availability; expiry does not rewrite who decided or imply a missed business review.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R13 — One durable input and admission effect
evidence.text:
### D19-R13 — One durable input and admission effect

Use the canonical accepted-input identity and its source generation, with a separately recorded review-decision sequence. Provider retries, duplicate webhook IDs, repeat commands and worker retries must reconcile that input's single current admission result. One source may legitimately map to permitted recipient occurrences under D1; never duplicate a conversation/message merely because a transport request ID changed. Atomically commit the review decision, source version and durable dispatch/outbox obligation. Canonical Support admission atomically commits its own source linkage/custody and receipt once. If a shared database permits one transaction, use it; otherwise keep the durable intermediate state and reconcile by authoritative effect identity. No provider I/O occurs inside the transaction. The stable admission-effect identity belongs to the canonical input and each D1-qualified recipient occurrence; source/gate revisions, review decisions and attempt IDs are fences and lineage, not reasons for another admission effect. Cancel release invalidates its pending decision/continuation generation. A later eligible release records a new decision and attempt against the same stable admission-effect identity: old canceled workers cannot act, and an earlier canceled attempt cannot permanently suppress valid re-release.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R17 — Concurrency and expired authority
evidence.text:
### D19-R17 — Concurrency and expired authority

Release, Dismiss, Return to review, gate changes, destination changes, permission revocation and admission/expiry share current source-version guards and a defined serialization point. Stale decisions conflict with a readable current outcome instead of overwriting. At an exact content deadline, admission is forbidden; admission must commit strictly before the deadline. A later fetch, retry, browser tab, route repair or policy lengthening cannot rehydrate expired content. Outbox replay rechecks current gates, content frontier and approved scope before positive effects. At admission the decision must remain qualified for its deciding actor/designation and current source/destination; the worker's service privileges do not substitute. Revocation before admission blocks the pending effect and records an owned current outcome. Admission that already committed retains truthful historical attribution, with current restrictions governing subsequent access/effects. Use the qualified owner fences, not a new global platform version counter. A worker cannot dismiss/expire a source using an obsolete policy version. Missing proof fails closed for that effect, with an accountable recovery state; uncertainty is not fabricated success.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R18 — Correct a mistaken release truthfully
evidence.text:
### D19-R18 — Correct a mistaken release truthfully

Before canonical admission commits, a qualified **Cancel release** may stop a pending release through the same current source guard. If admission has committed or cannot yet be reconciled, the UI must not promise Undo or deletion: reconcile first, then offer the authorized conversation/source correction path. Existing D9/D10/D16 owner commands handle wrong links, actual duplicates or unsafe admitted content; stop unsafe pending effects through their actual owner. Never unsend mail, erase valid staff work, delete CRM facts or make a delivered message disappear to simulate reversal. Preserve original review and correction evidence. A later security restriction always applies even if the earlier decision was legitimate.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R20 — Expiry, holds and copy custody
evidence.text:
### D19-R20 — Expiry, holds and copy custody

At the ordinary cutoff, end routine content visibility and release/recovery authority even if cleanup workers lag; record **Expired before admission** or the actual dismissed-expired outcome. Admission approval alone cannot establish a new D17 lifetime: only actual qualified Support admission/custody strictly before cutoff can do so, with its truthful readiness event. Dispose redundant intake copies under their actual transient-copy schedule; do not retain duplicate MIME forever after admission. Cleanup retires only the redundant occurrence/copy, never a shared authoritative blob still needed by the admitted source or another qualified owner.

Phase 26 owns the meaning of its intake schedule; the Phase 21 catalog does not classify intake or become its semantic owner. Reuse D16 source restriction and the existing qualified records/private-byte execution mechanisms for disposal and restore barriers to bodies, headers, safe previews, attachments, derived text, review exports, caches and retained provider copies. A legal/records/security preservation obligation can retain remaining required bytes in restricted custody without ordinary review access; unknown preservation blocks destruction and raises an owned exception, not an unlimited Reveal. Do not claim physical deletion, provider recall or backups erased until independently proved. Provider-retained bytes cannot become a rehydration route. Before live activation, every retained class/copy must have an owner, finite normal horizon, hold behavior, recovery boundary and disposal evidence contract; an unqualified class blocks its activation rather than being silently omitted.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R21 — Honest clocks and downstream eligibility
evidence.text:
### D19-R21 — Honest clocks and downstream eligibility

Keep first qualified provider receipt, first durable platform acceptance, gate/readiness transitions, review decision, canonical Support-ready admission and processing outcome separately. D14 reply-target time starts at its qualified source-ready event; queue age remains visible so a review delay cannot be concealed. Do not backdate readiness to provider receipt or reset original age to release time. D13 automatic request confirmation remains eligible only under its original rules and strictly before qualified first provider receipt plus 15 minutes; review never starts a new utility window, clears automation/loop suppression or creates a second confirmation. Reviewing, dismissing or admitting input is not a human reply, resolution, satisfied business action or achieved target.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R22 — CRM continuity and minimum necessary context
evidence.text:
### D19-R22 — CRM continuity and minimum necessary context

Held input is not an ordinary CRM conversation/communication row and must not update last-contact, create or merge a Party, establish a related-record association, assert verified identity, or perform a CRM mutation automatically, register a user, change consent or verify an address. Authorized read-only identity lookup follows the existing owner semantics; a candidate never establishes person identity, representation or a related-record association. D9-R02 correspondence eligibility still requires genuinely admitted source-message evidence and is not created by a held-item lookup. An eligible reviewer may open already-authorized CRM context when necessary through the normal owner surface; recognizing a correspondent is not permission to expose their giving, location or care data. On actual admission, D1/D2 identity distinctions and D9 qualified source-backed CRM discovery apply exactly once. Requester, message participant, authenticated user, CRM Party/relationship, assigned worker, reviewer and CRM owner remain distinct. CRM merge/deletion/link changes never rewrite original evidence or trigger re-ingestion. No synchronization between two Asym-owned CRM copies is introduced. Actual financial, receipt, recurring-gift, contact or care actions retain their domain permissions, approvals and truthful histories.

evidence.heading: ### D19-R23 — Email Studio, Resend and attention
evidence.text:
### D19-R23 — Email Studio, Resend and attention

Review UI is not an email composer. Keep D18's ratified Email Studio ownership of reusable content and prepared human replies, and D13's separate qualified **Support request received** template. Intake Release/Dismiss/Retry use neither a canned reply nor an ad hoc email template. Resend remains the qualified receiving provider; tenant/provider authority must be proven before fetch/replay, and Phase 6 remains the only external dispatch/evidence owner. Raw provider URLs and connection secrets stay server-side.

Use the shared in-product attention capability for coverage failure, aged unresolved review and expiring unresolved content; qualify a bounded source meaning and the existing source-actionable presentation policy before enabling it. Group by tenant/inbox/condition and reauthorize at display. Read/archive is not source completion. Default reviewer attention is in-product with no per-message email, external sender notification, push/body digest or dedicated notification engine. Any later authorized email channel must use an exact Email Studio meaning/template plus P6/tenant Resend; it cannot be assembled by a queue worker or extend source lifetime.

evidence.heading: ### D28-R04 Eligibility is source-owned
evidence.text:
### D28-R04 Eligibility is source-owned

A genuine ordinary Resolved completion can create a generation-bound candidate while the policy and inbox are enabled. At maturity, current source facts must still show completed ordinary work, an admitted external human request, qualified actual human email correspondence with that recipient, and a currently qualified recipient/send basis. A known accepted human reply establishes only transport evidence, not human receipt or satisfaction. Unresolved submission, missing authority, No response endings, spam/auto-only intake, drafts, internal-note-only work, restricted care content, suppressed endpoints and manual-only work lacking actual qualified email do not establish eligibility. A caller-supplied closure intent is not completion evidence: still-owed Support commitments and actionable unreviewed recovery block it under the existing owner rules. No arbitrary minimum message count or AI judgment substitutes for these facts. Exclusions and the email-only population limit are reported honestly.

evidence.heading: ### D28-R05 Candidate, opportunity and quiet interval
evidence.text:
### D28-R05 Candidate, opportunity and quiet interval

Completion creates a candidate with original conversation identity, exact resolution generation, frozen policy revision/percentage and due_at = genuine completion admission time + 24 elapsed hours. Reopening or relevant new admitted input before maturity invalidates that generation; later genuinely completed work can start a new candidate if no opportunity has been sampled. At mature admission, atomically create the one durable opportunity per original conversation and its sampling decision. After a draw, reopening or relevant new input cancels every definitely-unsubmitted invitation from that generation; the original opportunity stays consumed and later completion cannot resurrect the selected result. Old callbacks cannot sample a newer generation. Do not backdate a draw or apply a worker's processing-time percentage to an older candidate.

evidence.heading: ### D28-R09 Current gates and full invitation Off
evidence.text:
### D28-R09 Current gates and full invitation Off

Off fences every new or definitely-unsubmitted optional invitation without waiting for cancellation fan-out. Clear queued presentation through idempotent cleanup, but the current policy/source epoch is authoritative at the P6 boundary. Scope removal applies the same rule for that inbox. Existing submitted/possibly-submitted evidence remains truthful; issued response authority retains its original expiry unless its own privacy/safety source is revoked. The Off UI explains both facts. Off→On never resurrects cancelled generations or samples old completed history. Ordinary Support replies, intake and owner work remain available independently. A human reply to the invitation uses D1/D25’s qualified source/thread correlation and current intake; it is actual correspondence, not a rating submission. If original content is unavailable, existing source-safe intake applies without resurrection or email-only CRM matching.

evidence.heading: ### D28-R11 Merge, Undo and historical conservation
evidence.text:
### D28-R11 Merge, Undo and historical conservation

Keep immutable original conversation/opportunity/effect identities. Before sampling and submission, serialize against current D10 topology. If multiple unsampled candidates belong to one current component, select one neutrally eligible representative by earliest genuine completion instant then stable original ID and admit only its draw. Any prior component opportunity, including Not selected, prevents another original supplying a new chance. Record an immutable linked-suppression disposition for each otherwise eligible losing original, referencing that original opportunity without a fresh draw; Undo cannot revive it. Two independently committed pre-merge draws remain historical facts. A component with a prior possible/submitted invitation suppresses pending duplicates. If independent pending invitations merge, retain one deterministically by earliest genuine completion instant then original stable ID and suppress others. Two invitations submitted before their conversations merged remain two historical facts; no history rewrite or recall fiction. Undo alone creates no invitation, restores no cancelled generation and grants no new draw. CRM Party merging is distinct from Support merging and cannot create or transfer sampling authority.

evidence.heading: ### D28-R24 Honest measurement
evidence.text:
### D28-R24 Honest measurement

Report completion candidates/basic exclusions, matured eligible opportunities, selected/not selected, post-selection suppression reasons, submission-may-have-begun, accepted/unknown/failed/delivered evidence and submitted responses as distinct units. Invitation cohort dates are explicit; response-date browsing is distinct from cohort conversion. Preserve original effect counts after merges and show currently permitted original inbox/cohort provenance. Define issued as distinct invitation effects whose submission may have begun. Response fraction is unique responded-issued invitations divided by that same issued cohort, including indeterminate submissions; it never divides all responses only by provider-confirmed acceptances. Present counts and distribution of the three choices; if showing satisfied-share, define Satisfied / all non-excluded submitted ratings and show its denominator. No response is not positive or negative. Sampling is random among qualified opportunities, not all donors or unique people; frequency/eligibility exclusions and voluntary response mean no representativeness or margin-of-error claim. Do not offer employee leaderboards or cross-vendor benchmark comparison.

# Retained Support responsibility and shared internal work

**Status: Fully founder-ratified, 11 September 2026.** The founder selected A — keep the Support coordinator; delegate the internal action — on 11 September 2026. **Disposition: Accept with required amendments.** The founder fully accepts the complete D11 amendment package below, including every adopted amendment, addition, adjustment, change and update. D1–D10 remain fully ratified and unchanged. This is a grooming ADR, not implemented behavior or a formal specification.

Support retains its current handler or responsible shared inbox while a separately authorized person/team performs a bounded internal action. “Coordinator” describes existing responsibility, not a new role or automatic claim. Reuse the exact existing owner operation/task when it already represents that work; otherwise create one qualified shared Mission Control task. The source connection represents Support's need and review of a result, not a copy of task status, destination or business truth.

## Why this shape

Whole-conversation transfer remains the stronger alternative when the specialist should conduct the remaining requester exchange. Quick clarification can use a permitted internal note/mention, and already-authorized direct action needs no delegation ceremony. For a bounded specialist step, retained coordination avoids an unnecessary donor-facing handoff. The governing shared-task requirement makes a new Support child-ticket engine the wrong permanent path.

The present persisted task helper is contribution-oriented and ties assignment to its initiating actor. Separate task/link/history calls and generic in-memory Tasks UI are not a ready Support integration. Extend the actual shared owner command and closed source contracts; do not disguise Support work as Finance or swap actor IDs to assign a specialist.

## Required boundaries and current work

Keep the trusted initiator separate from Support handling, task queue/assignee and actual owner-action performer. Give specialists a minimal purpose-authorized task brief without granting the full Support transcript or CRM/finance/care access. Safe owner results can return to Support without exposing whole restricted tasks. Source-derived content retains its disclosure floor; free-text authoring is not an automatic declassification path.

Admit work/brief/source interests/receipt/history/required dispatch atomically in the shared owner boundary. One stable occurrence reconciles identical retries; changed meaning conflicts. Bind exact existing work rather than fuzzy title/Party/gift matches, and evaluate its current result immediately so reuse of completed work cannot wait forever. There is no blanket semantic dedupe of independent free-text requests.

Original source scope, owner target and purpose remain fixed within each interest generation. Revisions needing different meaning require a reviewed new generation. Multiple source interests may rely on one task. D10 merge/Undo composes or partitions current interests without copying work, resetting owner status or repeating an action. One owner occurrence produces one review per current handling component while preserving all affected contributions.

Asking for help preserves D3 work/reminder unless staff explicitly select a valid new plan. Task due and Support reminder stay distinct. Relevant input, results, missed promised work or adverse correction create current review; routine progress does not mirror task states into Support. Review acknowledges the exact owner result considered; it is not a task checkbox, financial approval, requester reply or Support resolution. Legitimate independent owner work may continue after Support has finished its obligation.

Stop following this work ends only the conversation's current interests. Optional task dismissal is a separate explicitly selected owner-authorized effect; no generic Support action cancels an independent refund or shared operation. The resulting D3 plan is revalidated so ending the last blocker cannot leave invalid Waiting; this work-specific label is distinct from D5's End follow-up. Historical references and permitted reliance evidence remain. A late duplicate cannot resurrect ended work, while a genuinely relevant correction of a relied-on result can require review.

## Coherent UI, notifications and CRM

Keep Internal note/mention, Ask for help and the existing assignment/transfer control distinct. Use a small contextual panel with visible current responsibility, relevant existing work, concise brief and eligible destination; disclose dates/details only when needed. One compact Internal work card shows actual owner progress and clear Result ready/Needs input review actions. The ordinary reply remains D2/D4/P17/P6/Resend, with no automatic recipient expansion or task-completion email.

Use qualified shared notifications for actual current recipients, not a duplicate Support alert producer or a fictional P6 queue recipient. Equal assignee IDs cannot suppress an unseen required result. Required queue work survives notification failure. Actual staff in-product/email evidence follows P6/P17 and never becomes donor correspondence merely through a Support source link. In-flight authorized email is not recalled by ending a task.

CRM retains D9 peer context/correspondence and one current Support conversation projection. Shared tasks and business actions retain their owner history, while actual communication retains P6 history. No new Party, fake donor interaction, copied task state or last-contact update is created. All read/write/egress paths preserve tenant/source/owner authority and current revocation.
